extracted.intended_audience: AISTATS 2023 reviewers and meta-reviewers (conference paper reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for reviewing submissions to the AISTATS 2023 conference: how to evaluate significance, correctness, clarity, reproducibility, ethics, and how to fill the review form and score submissions. Includes procedural notes for handling supplementary materials and code links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the review / reviewer role
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of the review process is twofold: (1) to identify papers which offer significant contributions to the fields of artificial intelligence and statistics for attendees and readers, and (2) to provide constructive feedback to authors that they can use to improve their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reviewing, always think about the long-term impact: out-of-the-box ideas, novel problems, and 'bridging fields' contributions are crucial. Novel or interdisciplinary works can be easy to criticize; be aware of bias and avoid dismissive criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary and contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly summarize the paper and its contributions: summarize motivation, key contributions and achievements in a paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although this part may not provide new information to authors, it is invaluable to Area Chairs and Program Chairs, and helps authors determine whether there are misunderstandings that need addressing in the author response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the strengths of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical criteria include soundness of the claims (theoretical grounding, empirical evaluation), significance and novelty of the contribution, and relevance to the AISTATS community. Cite relevant prior works when assessing significance. Consider how much researchers or practitioners will use or be influenced by the ideas. Solid technical papers exploring new territory or pointing out new directions can be preferable to incremental advances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the limitations of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on limitations according (but not limited) to soundness of claims (theory, empirical evaluation), significance and novelty, and relevance. Provide detailed, specific, and polite comments; avoid vague or dismissive complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correctness
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the claims and method correct? Is the empirical methodology correct?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain any incorrectness; incorrect claims or methodology are the primary reason for rejection. Be detailed, specific and polite; thoroughly motivate criticism so authors can understand and respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the paper clearly written? Does it clearly state its contributions, notation and results?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess organization and whether the submission adequately informs the reader. If not clear, make constructive suggestions for improvement. A superbly written paper provides enough information for an expert reader to reproduce its results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it clearly discussed how this work differs from or relates to prior work in the literature?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain whether the submission is written with due scholarship and suitably relates to prior work. The related work section should not just list prior work but explain how the proposed work differs from, builds upon, and/or improves on it. Note: authors are not expected to know about all non-peer-reviewed work; works appearing less than two months before the deadline are considered concurrent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional comments (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional field for additional comments, feedback and suggestions for improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add any further questions for authors, suggestions for improvement, or other optional comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there enough details to reproduce the main results of this work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the paper and supplementary material provide sufficient information to reproduce the main results. Lack of reproducibility should be listed among the weaknesses of the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumptions and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper explicitly and clearly state the main assumptions and limitations of the work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether assumptions and limitations are clearly stated in the paper and supplementary material. If not, consider listing this as a weakness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Societal impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper discuss the societal impact of the work, including impact from potential misuse?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the paper discusses potential societal impacts. If the nature of the research suggests it should, but it does not, note that in the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code release promise
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the authors promise to release code for this submission?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors promise to release code (anonymized link or included supplementary code), mark 'Yes'. Accepted papers that promise code are conditionally accepted and must release code publicly by the camera-ready deadline; reviewers help identify such papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Score (1–10)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Overall Score' reflects your assessment of the submission's contributions. Do NOT adjust scores to match conference acceptance rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the numeric definitions: 1 = Trivial or wrong or already known results; 2 = Strong reject (I would be very upset if accepted); 3 = Clear reject (I vote and argue for rejection); 4 = Reject (an ok submission but not good enough); 5 = Marginally below the acceptance threshold (lean reject but would not be upset if accepted); 6 = Marginally above the acceptance threshold (lean accept but would not be upset if rejected); 7 = Accept (a good submission); 8 = Clear accept (a very good submission, top 50% of accepted AISTATS papers); 9 = Strong accept (an excellent submission, top 15% of accepted AISTATS papers); 10 = Must accept (top 5% of accepted AISTATS papers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence score (1–5)
rubrics_metrics.description: How confident are you in your assessment?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1 = educated guess; 2 = willing to defend but likely unfamiliar/didn't check details; 3 = fairly confident (possible gaps, math not carefully checked); 4 = confident but not absolutely certain; 5 = absolutely certain, very familiar with related work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical concerns flag
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the submission raise potential ethical concerns? (Yes/No)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag methods, applications or data that create or reinforce unfair biases or have a primary purpose of harm or injury. This rating should be independent of your overall score; if 'Yes', briefly explain in the Ethical Concerns Details field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical concerns details
rubrics_metrics.description: If ethical concerns are flagged, briefly explain the potential concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise explanation of the ethical risks, biases, misuse potentials, or harms that motivated the flag.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of conduct agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Agree to abide by the AISTATS Code of Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must agree to the conference code of conduct linked from the guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must keep the paper and supplementary materials (including code and LaTeX source) and reviews confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes deleting any submitted code at the end of the review cycle to comply with confidentiality requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential comments to Area Chair
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional confidential field for Area Chair (not visible to authors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for explicit comparisons to other submissions or blunt criticisms. If you accidentally learn author identities, do not divulge them. You may include comments that should not be shared with authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practices for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Guiding behaviors reviewers should follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be thoughtful (don't crush spirits of inexperienced authors), be fair (do not let personal feelings affect review), be useful (helpful to authors, other reviewers, and ACs), be specific (avoid vague statements), be flexible (update review during discussion), be timely (respect deadlines). If pressured to give a particular score, notify Program Chairs; if you notice unethical behavior, notify your Area Chair.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to access and download assigned papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural steps to access assigned submissions via the CMT portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Login with reviewer CMT email, select 'Reviewer' role to see assignments. Download assigned papers via 'Actions -> Download Files'. The reviewing process is double-blind so you will not see author information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor formatting issues policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling of minor formatting inconsistencies in submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor formatting issues (e.g., different citation styles) should not be desk-rejected. Flag them but do not change your score or evaluation; the correct style will be ensured if the paper is accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplement / extra pages handling
rubrics_metrics.description: How to treat supplementary materials mistakenly appended to the main PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors forgot to separate supplementary pages from the main paper, treat extra pages as supplementary material. Looking at supplementary materials is optional for reviewers (as stated in the Call for Papers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Links in submission (external URLs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on external links included in submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The conference cannot guarantee the safety of external links. Recommendation: do not follow such links; take them as a statement that authors are ready to make material available if accepted. If you decide to access a link, be aware it might reveal your identity as a reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymous GitHub / code access guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: How to handle anonymous GitHub links or submitted code repositories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewing code is optional. If accessing anonymous GitHub links, directly download or clone the repository after logging out of your GitHub account; do not fork the repository as that may reveal your identity. Beware that submitted code may contain security vulnerabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting coercion or unethical/suspect behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: What to do if someone pressures you about a review or you notice unethical behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If pressured to provide a specific positive or negative review, notify the Program Chairs immediately at aistats2023@gmail.com. If you notice unethical or suspect behavior, notify your Area Chair right away.
